title: utv package use cases
description: What an application developer does with the Python library, step by step, with the branches the code has.

entities.name: Create a date
entities.description: A developer makes a date from its fields or from text, and learns why it can't exist when it can't (tasks a-date and feb-30).
entities.goal: Hold a calendar date, such as 5 November 2026, or a reason why the fields or text name no date.
preconditions: utv is importable: installed from implementations/python, or on the path with PYTHONPATH=src.
postconditions: The developer holds an immutable CivilDate whose year is any Python int, or an outcome or OutcomeError whose diagnostic code says why there is no such date.
Nothing was read from the machine: no clock, zone or locale.

flow.action: Calls CivilDate.of(2026, 11, 5) (or CivilDate(2026, 11, 5)); try_of with the same fields to get an outcome instead of an exception; or CivilDate.parse("2026-11-05") / utv.parse(text) for text.
For text, reads the ISO date grammar: YYYY-MM-DD, or a sign and four or more year digits.
Builds the date's UTV JSON and checks it: proleptic Gregorian calendar, month 1–12, day within that month of that year.
Returns the CivilDate; try_of and parse return Unique(CivilDate). str(date) is 2026-11-05.

alternatives.condition: A field isn't an int, such as the year "2026".
The text isn't in the grammar, such as "next Tuesday".
The text is a week date, an ordinal date or basic format (2026-W45-4, 2026-309, 20261105).
The text is a value of another type, such as 2026-11 for CivilDate.parse.
The day doesn't exist in that month: 30 February, or 29 February in a common year or a century not divisible by 400.
alternatives.outcome: of raises OutcomeError, a ValueError, carrying invalid and day-out-of-range; try_of and parse return Invalid (day-out-of-range).

alternatives.condition: The month is outside 1–12.

entities.name: Add months to a date
entities.description: A developer adds months (or years) to a date whose day may be missing from the target month (task month-end).
entities.goal: Get the date n months later, or learn that it doesn't exist and choose what to do.
preconditions: utv is importable: installed from implementations/python, or on the path with PYTHONPATH=src.
The developer holds a CivilDate, CivilDateTime or ZonedIntent.
postconditions: The developer holds the later value, or NoneOf (month-end) and no date was invented.
A clamped date appears only when the developer passed MonthEnd.CONSTRAIN.

flow.action: Calls date.add_months(1) (or add_years(n), or add(Period(months=1))).
Adds 12 × years + months to the year and month, through the JSON layer's add.
Checks that the day exists in the target month.
Adds any weeks and days, then hours, minutes and seconds as wall-clock time, and reads the result back as a typed value.
Returns Unique(date), such as 31 January + 2 months = Unique(2026-03-31).

alternatives.condition: The developer passes MonthEnd.CONSTRAIN (or "constrain") to add_months or add_years.
alternatives.outcome: The day is clamped to the month's last day and the date itself is returned, not an outcome: 31 January + 1 month = 2026-02-28.

alternatives.condition: The developer passes MonthEnd.REJECT or any other policy to the policy form.
alternatives.outcome: ValueError: rejecting is what the call without a policy does.

alternatives.condition: add(period) on a CivilDate with hours, minutes or seconds.
The day is missing from the target month (31 January + 1 month), and no policy, or REJECT with add(period), was given.
alternatives.outcome: NoneOf (month-end); its message names the month and the missing day.

alternatives.condition: The value is a ZonedIntent with an asserted offset.
alternatives.outcome: The result drops the asserted offset, which described the old wall time (offset-assertion-dropped in the JSON layer).

entities.name: Resolve a wall time in a zone
entities.description: A developer turns a wall time in an IANA zone into an instant under explicit zone rules, including in a DST gap or overlap, and sees an instant in another zone (tasks meeting-in-paris, dst-gap, dst-overlap).
entities.goal: Know which instant a wall time such as 09:00 in Paris names, or that it names none or two, and decide by policy.
preconditions: utv is importable: installed from implementations/python, or on the path with PYTHONPATH=src.

The developer has a rule bundle in the format of conformance/rules/demo-zones.json. The package ships none; the repository's demo bundle covers America/New_York, Europe/Paris and Atlantic/Reykjavik for 2026 and 2027.
postconditions: The developer holds Unique(Instant), Multiple of both instants, or an outcome saying why there is none; to_result() names the rule set used.
Nothing was read from the host's tz database.

flow.action: Loads the rules with ZoneRules.load(path) or ZoneRules.parse(text).
Makes a TemporalContext(rules); there is no default one.
Makes the intention: CivilDateTime.of(2027, 6, 1, 9, 0).in_zone("Europe/Paris").
Calls zoned.resolve(ctx), or resolve(ctx, ResolutionPolicy(gap=…, overlap=…)).
Looks the zone up, checks the wall time is at least a day inside the rules' window, and keeps every t = wall time − offset at which the zone's offset is that offset.
If the value asserts an offset, keeps only the candidate with that offset.
With one candidate, answers Unique(Instant); otherwise applies the gap or overlap policy.
Optionally sees the instant in another zone: instant.in_zone("America/New_York", ctx) gives 2027-06-01T03:00:00-04:00[America/New_York].

alternatives.condition: The bundle is malformed, or its transitions are out of order or beyond ±18:00.
Something other than ZoneRules, such as a path, is passed.
The zone id isn't shaped like Area/Location.
The zone isn't in the rules.
The wall time is within a day of either end of the rules' validity window.
alternatives.outcome: Unsupported (outside-rule-window): the rules are never extrapolated.

alternatives.condition: No candidate has the asserted offset, a wall time in a gap included.
No candidate: the wall time falls in a gap (02:30 on 8 March 2026 in New York), with Gap.REJECT (the default) or PRESERVE_UNRESOLVED.
A gap with Gap.SHIFT_FORWARD.
alternatives.outcome: Unique: the wall time minus the offset before the gap, so 02:30 gives the instant labelled 03:30 EDT.

alternatives.condition: Two candidates: the wall time falls in an overlap (01:30 on 1 November 2026 in New York), with Overlap.REJECT (the default).
alternatives.outcome: Multiple of both instants, ascending, with ambiguous; with Overlap.ALL, the same without a diagnostic.

alternatives.condition: An overlap with Overlap.EARLIEST or LATEST.
alternatives.outcome: Unique: the first or the second instant.

alternatives.condition: The zone isn't in the rules, or the instant is outside their window.

entities.name: Order two values
entities.description: A developer asks which of two values comes first: with operators for values of one type, and through a TemporalContext for zoned values, where the answer may be both (task compare-dates).
entities.goal: Know whether one value is before, equal to or after another, or that it depends on which side of a DST overlap is meant.
preconditions: utv is importable: installed from implementations/python, or on the path with PYTHONPATH=src.
For zoned values, a TemporalContext with rules covering both (as in resolve-a-zoned-time).
postconditions: The developer holds a bool for values of one type, or an Outcome[Ordering] listing every possible order for zoned values.

flow.action: Compares two values of one type with <, <=, > or >=: CivilDate(2026, 11, 5) < CivilDate(2026, 12, 25).
Compares their JSON with the JSON layer's compare: civil fields in order, with a missing second as 0; instants numerically; fixed-offset date-times by the instant they name.
When either value is zoned, calls ctx.compare(a, b) instead; a and b may be ZonedIntent, Instant or FixedOffsetDateTime.
Resolves each zoned value strictly, keeping both instants of an overlap.
Compares every candidate of a with every candidate of b; one possible order is Unique(Ordering).

alternatives.condition: The values are ZonedIntents.
alternatives.outcome: TypeError: ZonedIntent has no comparison operators, because its order depends on zone rules.

alternatives.condition: The values are of different types.
Two representations of the same time, such as CivilTime.of(9, 30) and CivilTime.of(9, 30, 0).
alternatives.outcome: <= and >= both hold and < doesn't, though the two are not equal: equality is equality of representation.

alternatives.condition: A wall time falls in a gap, or its zone or date is outside the rules, or its asserted offset contradicts them.
alternatives.outcome: NoneOf (gap), Unsupported (unknown-zone, outside-rule-window) or Invalid (offset-mismatch), passed on from resolve.

alternatives.condition: The order depends on which side of an overlap is meant: 01:30 and 01:45 on 1 November 2026 in New York.
alternatives.outcome: Multiple of the possible orders (BEFORE, EQUAL, AFTER as they occur), carrying the ambiguous diagnostic of each side that fell in the overlap.

entities.name: Convert to and from datetime
entities.description: A developer brings a datetime value, such as a clock reading, into UTV with a meaning they name, and takes a UTV value back out to datetime (tasks now and round-trip).
entities.goal: Use UTV alongside Python's datetime without any conversion guessing a meaning or losing something silently.
preconditions: utv is importable: installed from implementations/python, or on the path with PYTHONPATH=src.
For zoned values, a zoneinfo.ZoneInfo the developer made; its tz data is the host's, not UTV's.
postconditions: A round trip from datetime through UTV returns a value equal to the original.
Every refused or lossy conversion says so with a diagnostic code.

flow.action: Reads the clock themselves, since the library never does: datetime.now(timezone.utc), or time.time_ns() for Instant.from_unix_nanoseconds.
Calls utv.from_native(value, intent), for example from_native(reading, Intent.INSTANT).

Decides the meaning from the value and the intent: a naive datetime is a floating wall time; a fixed timezone is an INSTANT or an OFFSET; a ZoneInfo is ZONED by default, with the offset of its fold asserted; a timedelta is POSIX_SECONDS or a PERIOD.
Builds the UTV JSON and returns it as a typed value, such as Unique(Instant(2026-11-05T13:30:00Z)).
Calls utv.to_native(value, tz=…, allow_loss=…).
Converts to date, time, datetime or timedelta, checking range and precision; for a zoned value uses the tz passed, picking the fold from the asserted offset.

alternatives.condition: Anything but a date, time, datetime or timedelta.
A naive datetime asked for an INSTANT, OFFSET or ZONED, such as datetime.now() as an instant.
alternatives.outcome: Unsupported (local-zone): its meaning depends on the host's zone, which UTV never consults.

alternatives.condition: A datetime with a fixed timezone and no intent, a timedelta with no intent, or an unknown intent.
ZoneInfo("localtime"), a ZoneInfo from a file, or a tzinfo class that is neither timezone nor ZoneInfo.
A ZoneInfo wall time in a gap asked for an INSTANT or OFFSET.
alternatives.outcome: NoneOf (gap): Python would silently shift it.

alternatives.condition: A year outside 1–9999, or nanoseconds that aren't whole microseconds without allow_loss.
allow_loss=True and something had to be dropped.
alternatives.outcome: Unique, with a precision-loss or zone-dropped warning and the lost fields in the result's loss.

alternatives.condition: A ZonedIntent without tz.
alternatives.outcome: Unsupported (needs-zone-rules); with allow_loss and an asserted offset, a datetime with that fixed offset and zone-dropped.

alternatives.condition: A zoned wall time with no asserted offset that the tz says happens twice, or never.
alternatives.outcome: Multiple of the fold-0 and fold-1 datetimes, or NoneOf (gap).

alternatives.condition: A Period, ElapsedSeconds, CivilYearMonth or Interval.

entities.name: Write and read the text form
entities.description: A developer prints values as text and reads text back into typed values, including text from outside (task parse-offsets).
entities.goal: Show values in logs, documents and tests as text, and turn text into the value it describes without ever crashing on bad input.
preconditions: utv is importable: installed from implementations/python, or on the path with PYTHONPATH=src.
postconditions: str(v) is the text form wherever one exists, and utv.parse(str(v)) gives Unique(v) back.
Bad text produced an outcome with a diagnostic code, never an exception.

flow.action: Formats the value's JSON: points as ISO 8601 / RFC 9557, periods as ISO durations, intervals in brackets with explicit endpoint state.
Calls utv.parse(text), or T.parse(text) for one type.
Reads brackets, durations, EDTF slash intervals and ISO points: a trailing Z gives an instant, +00:00 a fixed offset of zero.
Returns the typed value the JSON describes, as Unique(value).

alternatives.condition: The value has no text form: a period with mixed signs, an instant at a third of a second.
alternatives.outcome: str prints the value's compact JSON instead.

alternatives.condition: The value is a PosixSeconds or ElapsedSeconds.
alternatives.outcome: str prints a display string, such as 3600.75 s (POSIX), which can't be parsed.

alternatives.condition: Text outside the grammar.
Week or ordinal dates, basic format, decimal period components, EDTF qualifiers such as 1347~, or an interval with no point.
Second 60 or 24:00.
Any annotation but one [Area/Location], or a [zone] after Z or -00:00.
An interval whose end is before its start, or whose ends differ in kind or form.
A field or offset out of range, such as 2026-02-30 or +19:00.
T.parse given text of another type.

entities.name: Validate UTV JSON and read it
entities.description: A developer checks UTV JSON received from elsewhere and reads it into typed values.
entities.goal: Accept only UTV JSON this library understands completely, and work with it as typed values.
preconditions: utv is importable: installed from implementations/python, or on the path with PYTHONPATH=src.
The developer has UTV JSON text or a parsed dict.
postconditions: The JSON is known to be structurally valid utv/1.0, and, if checked, to name a real Gregorian date; or the developer holds the reason it is not.
The developer holds the typed value, or knows the JSON needs the JSON layer.

flow.action: Calls validate_structural(text).
Parses the text rejecting duplicate keys and NaN, requires schema utv/1.0, and checks the value against the bundled schema.
Optionally calls validate_gregorian_date(text) to check that a civil value's fields name a real date.
Calls utv.from_json(json) or T.from_json(json) with the dict or the text.
Checks the value again, builds the typed value and makes sure it writes back exactly the same JSON.
Returns Unique(value); validate_structural returned status valid.

alternatives.condition: A key appears twice in an object.
The text isn't JSON, or holds NaN or Infinity.
A newer or other well-formed version, such as utv/1.1 or utv/2.0.
A malformed version label, such as utv/4.
An unknown kind or an unknown property.
The day doesn't exist; another calendar; another kind.
JSON text with a repeated key is given to from_json.
alternatives.outcome: json.loads keeps the last value and the repetition is not reported (backlog: from-json-text-duplicate-keys).

alternatives.condition: JSON of the wrong shape.
alternatives.outcome: Invalid (malformed-value), followed by the 0.1 structural codes.

alternatives.condition: T.from_json given another kind or form.
A valid value no typed value holds exactly: a zoned date, a resolutionPolicy, provenance, a recurrence.
alternatives.outcome: Unsupported (unsupported-operand); the JSON layer's functions still take it.
